arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Eisenhammer argued the case concerns whether a the side that brought the case may bring a Fourth Amendment claim for unlawful detention under legal process.
Ms. Eisenstein argued the Court should locate the constitutional right in the Fourth Amendment because it applies to pretrial detentions.
Mr. Scodro argued it is important to frame what is before the Court this afternoon.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case asks if the Fourth Amendment protects people from unreasonable seizure after legal process begins. the side that brought the case argues this protection continues until the detention ends. The city argues the protection stops once a judge approves the arrest.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants a court to recognize his right to sue for unlawful detention after a judge approves the arrest.
The city wants a court to deny his right to sue for detention that follows a judge's approval.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the Fourth Amendment applies to pretrial detentions and covers the time after legal process begins.
The city argues the Fourth Amendment claim ends when legal process begins, such as when a judge approves the arrest.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of constitutional protection against unreasonable government seizure. It determines when a person can seek legal redress for unlawful detention. The outcome shapes the balance between individual liberty and government authority in pretrial proceedings.
